title: Can One-sided Arguments Lead to Response Change in Large Language Models?
measurement_description: Evaluated the effectiveness of one-sided arguments in steering Large Language Model (LLM) responses on controversial (polemic) questions. The study's dataset included a 'Religious' category, which comprised 30% of the topics, to measure opinion change in this domain alongside historical and political topics.
findings: One-sided arguments were effective in changing LLM opinions across all topic classes, including religious ones. Political topics were most frequently 'convinced' (changed from neutral/negative to positive), followed by historical, and then religious topics. Conversely, for opinions that remained negative despite the one-sided arguments, religious topics were the most frequent, followed by historical, and then political, suggesting a higher baseline resistance to change on religious questions.
references: Gati Aher, Rosa I. Arriaga, and Adam Tauman Kalai. Using large language models to simulate multiple humans and replicate human subject studies. In Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning. JMLR.org, 2023.
